children: China could emerge as a competitor to Brazil in key chicken meat markets including the Middle East within the next decade after becoming a net exporter in 2025, Rabobank analyst Chenjun Pan told Reuters.
China is currently Brazil's top chicken export destination, but surging domestic production is generating exportable surpluses of cuts such as breast meat, which Chinese consumers rarely eat.
The world's fifth-largest chicken exporter in 2025, China shipped just over 1 million metric tons, according to Brazilian meat lobby ABPA.
Brazil, the top exporter, shipped 5.3 million tons.
Pan said potential competition in the Middle East, Asia and Africa could emerge within the next decade.
Chinese chicken production grew about 7% in 2025 and more than 9% year-on-year in the first half of 2026, Rabobank said.
Chinese chicken export destinations include Russia, Hong Kong, North Korea and Middle Eastern countries.
China does not compete with Brazil in the European Union, Japan or South Korea, where chicken vaccinated against bird flu is not accepted.
Beijing has promoted chicken production to reduce reliance on pork, following the African swine fever crisis of 2019–2021.
